title: ee.release_candidate_proof.v1
description: Content-addressed release-candidate proof capsule (bd-reality-core-convergence-1azkt.5). Binds, in one tamper-detecting record, the identities a release admission decision depends on: source tree, effective dependencies, toolchain, verification manifest, candidate binaries, test inventory, per-stage results, performance samples, CI/RCH run identifiers, and evidence hashes. THIS SCHEMA DEFINES THE SKELETON ONLY. `.5` emits a capsule that declares what it binds and what it has not established; `.19` is what populates a complete, green capsule for an immutable clean-main candidate. A capsule is therefore NOT a pass certificate: `completeness.populated` and `completeness.unestablished` are required precisely so an unpopulated skeleton cannot be mistaken for a verified candidate.

capsuleHash.description: Content address of every OTHER field of this capsule, canonicalized with sorted keys and this field omitted. Recomputing it over the received document is what makes the capsule tamper-detecting; a consumer that does not recompute it is trusting a string.

generatedAt.description: Emission time. Excluded from capsuleHash, because a capsule re-emitted over identical inputs must content-address identically.

completeness.description: The honesty field. A skeleton emitted by .5 sets populated=false and lists what it has not established; only .19 may emit populated=true. Absent this, an empty capsule and a verified one are the same shape. GREEN MUST REQUIRE AN EXPLICIT COMPLETENESS ASSERTION, NOT MERELY THE ABSENCE OF A FAIL. That is what this field exists to carry, and it is the requirement that would have caught every verification failure measured in this repo on 2026-09-17/18: verify.sh's pass line prints unconditionally; a CI Static badge means nothing without checking the run concluded, and 46 of 100 runs were cancelled by the next push; `cargo test --lib --test contracts` never reaches contracts when lib fails, so that target reports nothing; a run can exit 0 having executed zero tests (`0 passed; 484 filtered out`); a marker loop that returns on first mismatch reports one defect and never five. Every one of those greens was the ABSENCE OF A FAILURE rather than the PRESENCE OF A COMPLETED CHECK. So populated=true asserts that every declared stage REACHED a terminal verdict -- not that no stage reported FAIL.

populated.description: True only when every required binding carries real, verified content. A capsule with any placeholder, any unrun stage, or any unresolved identity MUST report false.

unestablished.description: Named things this capsule does NOT establish, each with the reason. A platform the host cannot build for belongs here, never silently omitted.

blockedBy.description: Tracker id when a specific bead or platform limitation owns the gap.

source.description: The tree the candidate was built from. `dirty` true is disqualifying for a release capsule and is recorded rather than refused here, so the refusal happens at admission with a reason.

effectiveDependencies.description: What was actually linked, not what the manifest requested. Franken-stack siblings are path dependencies whose resolved revision is not visible in Cargo.lock alone, which is why each is pinned explicitly.

manifest.description: Identity of the verification manifest this run executed. The stage registry is already pinned bijectively to verify.sh's run_stage calls by `verify_budget_manifest_declares_every_verify_stage`, so a capsule naming a different stage count than the registry is detectable.

binaries.description: Every candidate binary by identity, never by PATH lookup. A capsule that names a binary it did not hash is describing whatever happened to be installed.

testInventory.description: Exact inventory, so an omitted or duplicated logical test is visible. A logical test appearing in two shards is a defect, not redundancy.

results.description: Per-stage outcome using the SAME vocabulary verify.sh emits (STAGE_STATUS_VOCABULARY, scripts/verify.sh). One vocabulary across the runner and the capsule is the point: a capsule that invented its own status names would let 'did not run' and 'ran and passed' converge again at the release boundary.

attempts.description: Retry count. Retained so a stage that passed on attempt 4 is not reported identically to one that passed first time.

runIdentifiers.description: Run ids on both admission lanes. `hostedCi` is nullable and MUST be null rather than fabricated while the hosted workflows are disabled_manually (bd-o7wh0) — a capsule claiming a hosted run that did not happen is the failure this whole record exists to prevent.

evidenceHashes.description: Content addresses of the artifacts this capsule attests to. Repo-relative paths only: an absolute path is not reproducible across hosts and cannot be pinned.
